title: Output of the traitement-episode agent: an episode's treatment (its scenes)

scenes.description: In episode order, within the requested range (`nombreDeScenes`).

titre.description: (French) Distinct from every other scene's title.

fonction.description: (French) What the scene accomplishes in the episode.

genre.description: The scene's genre: it decides the cutting and the writing guides of its plans later. action: a physical gesture or a clash; dialogue: characters talking to each other; montage: a series of brief moments that answer each other; contemplatif: a place or a state left to breathe; tension: a build-up or a tipping point.

ambiance.description: (French) The visual frame HELD over the whole scene, in one sentence: time of day, weather, general light.

intention.description: (French) What the scene tells, in two or three narrative sentences: who does what, why, what changes. No framing, light, sound or camera movement.

etatEntree.description: (French) Where the scene starts: where the characters who matter are and what they face, relative to fixed landmarks of the place. The previous scene's etatSortie when the story goes on without a break.

etatSortie.description: (French) Where the scene ends, in the same terms. Only what the scene's story justifies.

poids.description: Screen time relative to the other scenes (1 transition, 5 key scene). Never seconds.

momentsDeLAuteur.description: (French) What the author said about THIS scene (gestures, framing, sounds, lines, ending), close to their words. Empty string if nothing.

inventions.description: (French) Everything that was not in the brief. To validate or throw out.

notes.description: (French) Risky choices, doubts about the cutting. Empty if nothing to report.
